clue.text: Hurried back to business with spasm — given drug

indicators.note: going back means the word for hurried is read from right to left

parts.note: hurried means ran
CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
a tic is an involuntary muscular spasm

explanation.surface: Someone rushing back to work with a twitch is handed some medication.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic is a drug that dulls the senses, such as opium or morphine.

clue.text: Tale is unusually neat — about code cracking

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first jumble wraps round the second
unusually means in an odd way, so the letters of neat are put in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: something cracking breaks apart, so the letters of code are rearranged too

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A neatly told story about breaking a secret code.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short, amusing account of a real incident, which is a kind of tale.

clue.text: Mate means to reach cabin thereby

definitions.note: describes the thing as a route: the way by which to reach a cabin

parts.note: a mate is a companion
a means is a way of doing something

explanation.surface: A ship's mate explains how to get down to a cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: Mate looks nautical, a ship's officer, but here it is just a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A companionway is the staircase on a ship leading from the deck down to the cabins below.

clue.text: Will maker try to up?

parts.note: to try something is to test it

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the scan reads 'to' here, but the answer needs rota, a duty roster; the printed word looks lost in the OCR

explanation.surface: A person drawing up a will is urged to try harder.
explanation.walkthrough: The scanned clue is faulty: the printed clue almost certainly read 'try rota up', with rota written upwards after the word for try.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is the person who makes a legal will leaving property to heirs.

clue.text: Whence the ray seen by gogglers?

definitions.text: Whence the ray seen by gogglers?

parts.note: surface reading: where does a beam of light come from
setter's reading: gogglers stare at the goggle-box, an old television, whose picture tube fires an electron beam from a negative electrode

explanation.walkthrough: Goggle-box is British slang for a television; old sets had a tube whose ray of electrons came from this electrode.
explanation.definitionFit: Cathode rays are electron streams emitted from a negative electrode, the source of the picture in old TV tubes.

clue.text: Algerian port gets half the fruit

parts.note: Oran is a large port city on Algeria's Mediterranean coast

indicators.note: half means only the first two of the four letters in gets are used

parts.note: the front portion of the word

explanation.surface: A North African harbour receives half its cargo of citrus.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange is a round citrus fruit with a tough bright skin, an everyday example of fruit.

clue.text: Famous Venetian game

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Marco, the merchant traveller who went to China
second meaning: a team sport played on horseback with mallets

explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo was the celebrated explorer from Venice, and the word also names the horseback ball sport.

clue.text: Need of a seer?

parts.note: surface reading: what a prophet requires, such as second sight
setter's reading: a seer is simply someone who sees, and they need working vision

explanation.walkthrough: Seer suggests a fortune-teller, but read literally it is anyone who sees.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who sees requires the faculty of vision, which this word names.

clue.text: Bitterness of a close friend about motorway return

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the friend's letters wrap round the motorway

parts.note: a crony is a close friend or pal

indicators.note: a return trip goes back the other way, so the motorway's name is read backwards

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A sour falling-out with a pal on the drive home along the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the London to Leeds motorway; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrimony is harsh, angry ill feeling between people, which is a kind of bitterness.

clue.text: Appear to view maid as helpless

indicators.note: help-less splits as minus the word for help, so that word comes out of the maid

parts.note: to view is to see
taken as written, before the help is removed

explanation.surface: A servant looks hopelessly incapable.
explanation.walkthrough: Helpless is read as help-less: AID, a word for help, is taken out of MAID, leaving M.
explanation.definitionFit: To seem is to give an outward impression, so it is a close synonym of to appear.

clue.text: Chucks the game,, perhaps
Modify Manet's varied dispositions

parts.note: to temper is to modify or moderate

indicators.note: varied means changed, so the letters of the painter's name are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Changing the moods of the French painter's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperaments are people's characteristic natures or moods, which is what dispositions means.

clue.text: Headwear overlooked by driver?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a hat tied under the chin
second meaning: the hinged engine cover a motorist looks over through the windscreen

explanation.walkthrough: Overlooked looks like 'ignored', but it is literal: the driver looks out over this part of the car. In American English it is the hood.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a brimmed hat tied under the chin and the hinged cover over a car engine.

clue.text: Fancies being retired, maybe

parts.note: surface reading: fanciful ideas about life after giving up work
setter's reading: having fancies while retired to bed, asleep, as one may when the lights are out

explanation.walkthrough: Retired suggests leaving work, but here it means gone to bed, where fancies come in sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: The fancies a sleeper has after going to bed are dreams, so having them is this activity.

clue.text: Roused by mistake about five, eats greedily

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the number
something put together by mistake is jumbled, so the letters of roused are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Someone woken in error at five o'clock wolfs down breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: To devour is to eat hungrily and quickly, gulping food down, which is eating greedily.

clue.text: Appointment with friend, Mr French, bears fruit

definitions.note: describes the answer by what it does: a tree that bears fruit

parts.note: a date is an appointment
a pal is a friend
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, the French for Mr

explanation.surface: A meeting with a pal and a Frenchman proves fruitful.
explanation.walkthrough: Bears fruit sounds like 'succeeds', but it is literal: the answer is something that produces fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A date palm is a tall tree that produces dates, so it is a thing that bears fruit.

clue.text: China and Japan are coming in quickly

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so the word for are goes inside the word for quickly

parts.note: fast means quickly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Chinese and Japanese exports are flooding in rapidly.
explanation.definitionFit: China and Japan are examples of countries in the eastern Asian region known collectively by this name.

clue.text: Marriage, a nice arrangement, gives 'everyone support

parts.note: everyone means all

indicators.note: an arrangement sets things in a new order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wedding, nicely arranged, gets everybody's backing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the jumbled letters sit below and support the word for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union or bond, and a marriage is an alliance between two people or families.

clue.text: Miss Cole corrects an absurdity

indicators.note: to correct something is to alter it, so the letters are changed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher fixes a ridiculous mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: Miss Cole sounds like the teacher marking the error; her name supplies the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A solecism is a blunder in grammar or etiquette, an incongruity that looks absurd to the observer.

clue.text: Smith's job to give direction on garden work

parts.note: S is south, a compass direction
hoeing is weeding a garden with a hoe

explanation.surface: Someone named Smith is tasked with directing the gardening.
explanation.walkthrough: Smith looks like a surname, but it is a blacksmith or farrier, who fits horseshoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrier or blacksmith fits iron shoes to horses, so this task is that tradesman's work.

clue.text: Value of little cap in Staffordshire town

parts.note: a tam is a soft Scottish cap, short for tam-o'-shanter
value means worth

explanation.surface: Pricing a small hat bought in a Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue puts value first, but the cap's letters come first in the answer, as 'value of' a cap reads cap then value.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamworth is a market town in Staffordshire, an English county in the West Midlands.

clue.text: Sell a litre after conversion

indicators.note: a conversion turns something into another form, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Selling a litre once it has been changed to metric.
explanation.definitionFit: To retail is to sell goods to the public in small quantities, rather than wholesale.

clue.text: Apt and responsible

definitions.meaning: first meaning: inclined or likely to do something
second meaning: legally answerable for something

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both likely to do something and legally answerable, as in being held accountable for a debt.

clue.text: Takes action in court, perhaps — behaves honourably

definitions.meaning: first meaning: competes on a tennis or squash court, not in a court of law
second meaning: acts fairly and by the rules

explanation.walkthrough: Takes action in court suggests suing someone; 'perhaps' flags that the court is a sports court where a match is under way.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes taking part in a sporting contest and idiomatically means acting fairly and decently.

clue.text: Jack to be given Provost's address

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
taken as written, without the to

explanation.surface: A sailor is told to adopt a grand title.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbé is the French title used in addressing a cleric, such as the provost of a church.

clue.text: Retired man among the clientele?

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the concealed letters are read from right to left
among means sitting within, so the answer lies inside the letters of the next word

parts.note: the run of letters in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: A pensioner sits among the customers.
explanation.walkthrough: Retired suggests a pensioner, but it tells you to read backwards: clIENTele hides NEIL reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil is a common male first name, and a crossword man is often any name.

clue.text: West African gives money to ancient European

parts.note: L stands for libra, the pound in old British money
the Iberians were an ancient people of Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: A man from West Africa hands cash to an old Spaniard.
explanation.definitionFit: A Liberian is a citizen of Liberia, a country on the coast of West Africa.

clue.text: Gin-opening general gets a little merry

indicators.note: an opening is the start, so only the first letter of gin is used

parts.note: the first letter of the drink
Robert E Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
a little means some

explanation.surface: A general who opens the gin becomes a bit tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Gleesome is an old literary word for full of glee, so it means joyful and merry.
